Changelog & service record

What changed, when, and what it means for relying parties.

Entries are append-only. A correction to an entry is a new entry — the original remains readable. Scheduled transitions (for example, a graduation date) are listed on the status page and are recorded here only when they happen. Machine-readable: changelog.json · RSS.
12 November 2026 · Added · Website, Status, Changelog, Practice

Status page, changelog, and practice page — one canonical source

The site now carries a status page generated from a single canonical status source (also published as status.json), this changelog with JSON and RSS feeds, and a practice page describing how releases are gated, soaked, and graduated, what a certificate does and does not claim, and how to report an error. Status facts — availability, lifecycle, dates, endpoints — are no longer typed independently into separate pages: the status page, status.json, the machine-readable service record, and the llms.txt status section are generated from the same source, and CI drift checks fail the build when they disagree. The former release log at /releases/ is now an alias of this changelog, and its entries were migrated here unchanged.

Effect: Anyone — customer, auditor, or agent — can read the current state of every surface in one place, including what is paused, in soak, in design, or not built.

Evidence: Status · Status JSON · Practice

Disposition: Live on the site; graduation of the surfaces it describes remains as recorded on /status/.

12 November 2026 · Documentation · Docs, How It Works, Pricing, Security, Release log, Blog

P0 closure: verdict taxonomy, pricing schema, security scope, status notes

The remaining P0 truth corrections landed. The verdict taxonomy is now stated the same way everywhere it appears: verdicts are boolean — PASSED or FAILED — and a request that ends before a verdict (payment required, timeout, concurrency/rate/size refusal, failed queued job) is a NO VERDICT error outcome, not a verdict; the retired INCOMPLETE wording is gone. The pricing JSON-LD now marks the credit packs OutOfStock — not yet on sale, matching the paused billing state the page already stated in prose. The Security page's in-scope list now names the hosted MCP endpoint, the web verifier, and the Ask shell. Until this changelog landed, the release log and the 2026-09-26 blog essay carried interim dated status notes; those notes are replaced by pointers to /status/ and this changelog. A 21-surface live evidence pack was filed with the change.

Effect: No known false claim remains on the site; every surface states the same taxonomy, the same billing state, and the same scope.

Evidence: Docs · Security · Pricing

Disposition: Closed. Claim-by-claim evidence verification continues under the status source's last-verified discipline.

11 November 2026 · Documentation · How It Works, Docs, Homepage, Terms, Security, llms.txt, .well-known

Material wording corrections

Public wording was corrected where it contradicted the service. The hosted MCP endpoint is live, and every surface that said otherwise — How It Works, Terms §1, the Security page, llms.txt, and the machine-readable service record — now says so. The Docs verdict table was corrected: a completed paid verification that returns FAILED receives a signed certificate recording FAILED (the table previously said no certificate is issued). Homepage copy that implied smart-contract verification is a current capability was removed or rewritten: that capability is in design (see /status/).

Effect: Human pages, paperwork, and machine-readable mirrors state the same facts about MCP availability, FAILED certificates, and smart-contract scope.

Evidence: How It Works · Docs

Disposition: Closed; verified live the same day.

Third-party signup promotion removed — ruled out fleet-wide

A third-party signup promotion found in product copy was removed the same day. The ruling is fleet-wide: no product carries a third-party signup promotion. A plain, unlinked credit line (“Built with Muse by Meta”) is not a promotion and remains.

Effect: No AxiomCode surface promotes a third-party signup.

Evidence: Homepage

Disposition: Closed; verified live the same day (zero matches for the promotion on the audited pages).

11 November 2026 · Finding · Web verifier, Certificate checker, REST API

Finding F-AX-10: browser submission repaired

Finding / Fixed. The flipped web verifier and certificate checker could render but could not complete a browser submission, because the production API lacked the required cross-origin (CORS) leg for the site origin. The defect escaped the public flip and was found in post-deploy verification. The repair added the scoped browser path (preflight and allow-origin for the site origin on /verify, /check, and /shell/turn; foreign origins receive nothing) and was verified from the site origin after deployment. F-AX-10 is closed.

Effect: Browser submissions on /verify/ and /check/ complete end-to-end; API-key callers were never affected.

Evidence: Gate declaration (gate.yaml) · Threat model · Security

Refs: F-AX-10

Disposition: Closed 2026-11-11 on the gate's post-deploy probes.

11 November 2026 · Added · Ask shell, Ask explanations

Ask shell launched

Added / Status. Ask entered production at axiom-code.com/ask/. Ask renders facts from the verification service and may add an explanation; it does not issue, change, soften, or predict verdicts — the Lean kernel remains the only judge. The shell is degraded-first: if the explanation step times out, the service facts are still returned and the missing explanation is stated. Ask is in release-candidate soak; its graduation decision is scheduled for 2026-11-18, and explanation latency is a known residual carried in the soak.

Effect: Conversational access to verification facts is live, with the fact/judgment boundary stated on the surface itself.

Evidence: Ask

Disposition: In soak; graduation decision scheduled 2026-11-18.

9 November 2026 · Added · REST API, Hosted MCP, Web verifier, Certificate checker, Trial

Public opening and hosted MCP

Added / Status. AxiomCode opened the REST verification service at api.axiom-code.com: POST /verify with an API key, POST /check, queued-job status, and the public revocation list and CA keys. The hosted MCP endpoint also entered production at https://api.axiom-code.com/mcp/ with seven tools: verify, job_status, check_certificate, revoked, health, usage_report, and pricing. Trial keys receive 10 verification cases — verdicts and usage records, no certificates. New with the opening: a durable FIFO verification queue — when every proof slot is busy, submissions answer 202 with a job id and a checkable position instead of competing for the engine. The flip package also lands the release-gate declaration for the service (gate.yaml, threat model, and coverage ledger in the repository). Billing remains paused: credit packs are not on sale, and the Stripe webhook and Payment Links remain deactivated until pack sales are deliberately opened. The public service and hosted MCP are in release-candidate soak; their graduation decision is scheduled for 2026-11-16.

Effect: The service is open to humans, applications, and agents; certificates unlock when pack sales open.

Evidence: API health · MCP endpoint · Gate declaration (gate.yaml)

Refs: F-AX-4, F-AX-5

Disposition: In soak; graduation decision scheduled 2026-11-16. (Migrated from the former release log, with the hosted-MCP record completed from the launch record.)
